headline: Individualized network models extend from brain parcellation to cerebral hemodynamics
label: Individualized Network Modeling
summary: Recent preprints pair subject-specific network modeling with cross-cohort benchmarks, exposing generalization limits in MRI segmentation.
synthesis: The dominant thread across these three preprints is individual-specific structure treated as both the object of analysis and the basis for modeling. IndivSTATIS applies a STATIS-based multivariate method to compare individualized brain parcellations and networks in a shared component space. The circulation preprint builds a multiscale model coupling systemic hemodynamics, cerebral autoregulation, and imaging-derived Circle of Willis networks to simulate flow under anatomical variation and stenosis. The MICCAI 2024 challenge report is less directly network-oriented: it benchmarks deep learning for enlarged perivascular space segmentation and reports that top methods degrade on an unseen cohort. Its link to the others is evaluative, centering on generalization beyond the training population. What is new is extending individualized network representations into vascular simulation alongside cross-subject comparison frameworks.
